soru:
Urban green spaces, such as parks and community gardens, offer far more than aesthetic value. Research has shown that people who live near green areas report lower levels of stress and are more likely to exercise regularly. In addition, trees help to reduce air pollution and lower temperatures during heatwaves. For these reasons, many city planners now regard green spaces as essential infrastructure rather than a luxury.

What is the main idea of the passage?
secenekler: Heatwaves have become more frequent in urban areas.
City planners are reluctant to invest in green spaces.
Community gardens are more popular than parks in most cities.
Regular exercise is the best way to reduce stress.
Green spaces provide important health and environmental benefits for cities.
aciklama: Parça yeşil alanların sağlık ve çevre yararlarını sıralayıp onların vazgeçilmez olduğu sonucuna varıyor; diğer seçenekler ya ayrıntı ya da metinde olmayan bilgiler.

soru:
For centuries, sailors relied on the stars to find their way across the oceans. By measuring the angle between a particular star and the horizon, they could calculate their latitude with reasonable accuracy. Determining longitude, however, remained a serious problem until the eighteenth century, when the invention of an accurate marine clock finally allowed navigators to compare local time with the time at their home port.

The passage is mainly about ----.
secenekler: the differences between latitude and the horizon
why sailors preferred travelling at night
how navigation methods at sea developed over time
the dangers of long ocean voyages in the eighteenth century
aciklama: Parça yıldızlarla enlem hesabından deniz saatiyle boylam hesabına uzanan yön bulma yöntemlerinin gelişimini anlatıyor.

soru:
Many people believe that multitasking allows them to get more done in less time. However, studies in cognitive psychology suggest the opposite. When people switch rapidly between tasks, their brains need time to readjust, which leads to more errors and slower overall performance. What feels like efficiency is, in reality, a series of small interruptions that reduce the quality of work.

Which of the following best states the main idea of the passage?
secenekler: Cognitive psychology has little to say about productivity.
Multitasking is less efficient than many people think.
The brain can easily handle several tasks at the same time.
Switching between tasks improves the quality of work.
People who multitask make fewer errors than others.
aciklama: 'However, studies ... suggest the opposite' cümlesi ana fikri verir: çoklu görev sanıldığı kadar verimli değildir.

soru:
Although antibiotics have saved millions of lives since their discovery, their overuse has created a new threat. Every time an antibiotic is used, bacteria that happen to be resistant survive and multiply. Over time, these resistant strains become dominant, making infections that were once easily treated potentially fatal. Health experts therefore stress that antibiotics should be prescribed only when they are truly necessary.

Which of the following best expresses the main point of the passage?
secenekler: Antibiotics are no longer effective against any kind of infection.
Resistant bacteria can only be found in hospitals.
The discovery of antibiotics was a mistake in the history of medicine.
The careless use of antibiotics contributes to the spread of resistant bacteria.
Health experts recommend using antibiotics to prevent all infections.
aciklama: Parçanın odağı aşırı antibiyotik kullanımının dirençli bakterileri yaygınlaştırmasıdır. 'no longer effective against any' gibi seçenekler aşırı genellemedir.

soru:
The Great Wall of China was not built in a single period. Construction began as early as the seventh century BC, when various states built walls to protect themselves from their neighbours. The best-known sections, however, date from the Ming dynasty (1368–1644), when the wall was rebuilt with bricks and stone to defend the empire against invasions from the north.

According to the passage, the best-known sections of the Great Wall ----.
secenekler: were built during the Ming dynasty
were built to protect states from each other
were destroyed by invasions from the north
were constructed in the seventh century BC
aciklama: 'The best-known sections, however, date from the Ming dynasty' cümlesi doğrudan cevabı verir.

soru:
Octopuses are remarkable for their ability to change colour in a fraction of a second. This is made possible by thousands of special cells called chromatophores, which contain pigments and are located just beneath the skin. By expanding or contracting these cells, an octopus can blend into its surroundings, warn predators or communicate with other octopuses.

According to the passage, chromatophores ----.
secenekler: are cells containing pigments that allow octopuses to change colour
help octopuses to breathe under water
take several minutes to change the colour of the skin
are found deep inside the octopus's brain
are used only to attract a mate
aciklama: Parçaya göre kromatoforlar derinin hemen altında bulunan, pigment içeren ve renk değişimini sağlayan hücrelerdir.

soru:
In 1928, the Scottish scientist Alexander Fleming returned from holiday to find that one of his bacterial cultures had been contaminated by a mould. He noticed that the bacteria surrounding the mould had been destroyed. Fleming identified the mould as Penicillium notatum, but it was not until the early 1940s that other scientists managed to produce penicillin in large quantities.

It is stated in the passage that Fleming ----.
secenekler: discovered penicillin while on holiday in Scotland
failed to identify the type of mould he had found
deliberately added mould to his bacterial cultures
noticed that the mould had killed the bacteria around it
produced penicillin in large quantities in 1928
aciklama: 'He noticed that the bacteria surrounding the mould had been destroyed' cümlesi doğru seçeneği destekler; büyük miktarda üretim 1940'larda başka bilim insanlarınca yapılmıştır.

soru:
Contrary to popular belief, camels do not store water in their humps. The humps actually contain fat, which can be broken down into energy when food is scarce. Camels survive in the desert thanks to several other adaptations: their kidneys conserve water efficiently, their body temperature can rise by several degrees before they start to sweat, and they can drink up to 100 litres of water in a short time.

According to the passage, which of the following is NOT true about camels?
secenekler: They can drink large amounts of water quickly.
They store water in their humps.
Their body temperature can rise before they start to sweat.
They can use their fat reserves as a source of energy.
aciklama: Parçanın ilk cümlesi develerin hörgüçlerinde su depolamadığını açıkça söyler; diğer seçenekler metinde doğrulanır.

soru:
When the first public libraries opened in Britain in the mid-nineteenth century, many members of the upper classes opposed them. They feared that giving ordinary workers free access to books would encourage them to question the existing social order. Supporters, on the other hand, argued that libraries would make workers more responsible citizens and reduce crime.

It can be inferred from the passage that ----.
secenekler: crime rates fell sharply after libraries were opened
libraries were closed after protests by the upper classes
public libraries were seen as having the power to influence society
the upper classes built the first public libraries
most workers in Britain were unable to read in the nineteenth century
aciklama: Hem karşıtlar (düzeni sorgulatır) hem destekçiler (suçu azaltır) kütüphanelerin toplumu etkileyebileceğini düşünüyordu. Diğer seçenekler metinde desteklenmez.

soru:
Some species of birds that migrate at night use the Earth's magnetic field to navigate. In laboratory experiments, when researchers altered the magnetic field around caged birds, the birds began to orient themselves in the wrong direction. However, when the natural magnetic field was restored, they quickly corrected their course.

It can be inferred from the passage that ----.
secenekler: birds cannot see the stars when they are kept in cages
all birds migrate during the night
caged birds never attempt to migrate
the Earth's magnetic field is getting weaker every year
changes in the magnetic field can confuse some migrating birds
aciklama: Manyetik alan değiştirilince kuşların yanlış yöne dönmesi, bu değişikliğin onları şaşırtabildiğini gösterir. 'all birds' aşırı genellemedir.

soru:
Maria had studied French for six years at school, but on her first visit to Paris she found that she could hardly understand what people were saying. The textbooks she had used had taught her formal language, whereas the people she met spoke quickly and used a great deal of slang.

It can be concluded from the passage that ----.
secenekler: Maria had never studied French before visiting Paris
people in Paris refused to speak French to tourists
the language taught in Maria's textbooks differed from everyday speech
formal language is more difficult to learn than slang
Maria's French teachers spoke too quickly
aciklama: Ders kitaplarının resmî dili öğretmesi ile insanların argo kullanması arasındaki fark, kitap dilinin günlük konuşmadan farklı olduğunu gösterir.

soru:
In the 1950s, the introduction of the rabbit disease myxomatosis to Australia killed more than 90 percent of the rabbit population within a few years. Yet within a few decades, rabbit numbers had largely recovered. Scientists discovered that the surviving rabbits had developed genetic resistance to the disease, while the virus itself had become less deadly over time.

It can be inferred from the passage that ----.
secenekler: all rabbits in Australia died in the 1950s
myxomatosis was introduced to Australia by accident
the virus became more deadly as rabbits became resistant
the attempt to control rabbits with a disease had only temporary success
rabbits are no longer considered a problem in Australia
aciklama: Tavşan sayısının önce düşüp birkaç on yılda toparlanması, hastalıkla kontrol girişiminin yalnızca geçici başarı sağladığını gösterir.

soru:
The drought lasted for three years and left the farmland barren. Nothing could grow in the dry, cracked soil, and many farmers were forced to leave the region in search of work.

The word 'barren' in the passage is closest in meaning to ----.
aciklama: 'Nothing could grow' ifadesi toprağın verimsiz ('barren' = unproductive) olduğunu gösterir; 'fertile' zıt anlamlıdır.

soru:
The new evidence seemed to corroborate the witness's account: the security camera showed the suspect entering the building at exactly the time she had described.

The word 'corroborate' in the passage is closest in meaning to ----.
aciklama: Kamera görüntüsü tanığın anlattığıyla örtüşüyor; 'corroborate' = doğrulamak (confirm).

soru:
Although the medication alleviated the patients' pain, it did not cure the underlying condition, and the symptoms returned as soon as the treatment was stopped.

The word 'alleviated' in the passage is closest in meaning to ----.
aciklama: 'Although ... it did not cure' zıtlığı, ilacın ağrıyı hafiflettiğini ('alleviate' = relieve) gösterir.

soru:
The minister's speech was deliberately ambiguous. Journalists could not tell whether she supported the proposed reform or intended to block it, and both sides claimed that she was on their side.

The word 'ambiguous' in the passage is closest in meaning to ----.
secenekler: open to more than one interpretation
aciklama: Gazetecilerin bakanın hangi tarafta olduğunu anlayamaması, konuşmanın birden fazla şekilde yorumlanabildiğini gösterir.

soru:
It is astonishing that, in the twenty-first century, millions of children still lack access to basic education. Governments that spend enormous sums on weapons can surely find the resources to build schools and train teachers. The problem is not a lack of money but a lack of political will.

The author's attitude towards governments can best be described as ----.
aciklama: 'It is astonishing', 'can surely find' ve 'a lack of political will' ifadeleri yazarın hükümetleri eleştirdiğini gösterir.

soru:
Social media platforms have undoubtedly made it easier for people to stay in touch. Yet we should not ignore their darker side: the spread of false information, the pressure to present a perfect life and the loss of privacy. A balanced view recognises both the benefits and the dangers.

The author's main purpose in the passage is to ----.
secenekler: persuade readers to stop using social media
explain how social media platforms make money
present a balanced view of social media
praise social media for spreading information
describe the history of social media
aciklama: Yazar önce yararları, sonra zararları sayıyor ve son cümlede dengeli bakışı savunuyor.

soru:
Visitors to the museum will find an impressive collection of ancient pottery, jewellery and tools. The exhibition is open every day from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m., and guided tours are available in five languages. Tickets can be purchased online or at the entrance.

The main purpose of the passage is to ----.
secenekler: inform visitors about a museum exhibition
explain how ancient pottery was made
aciklama: Metin saat, rehberli tur ve bilet bilgisi veriyor; amacı ziyaretçileri bilgilendirmektir.

soru:
Proponents of the new dam claim that it will provide cheap electricity for millions. What they rarely mention is that thousands of villagers will lose their homes and that a unique ecosystem will be destroyed forever. One wonders whether the promised benefits are worth such an irreversible cost.

It is clear from the passage that the author ----.
secenekler: strongly supports the construction of the dam
has serious doubts about the benefits of the dam
believes that villagers will benefit most from the dam
is mainly concerned with the price of electricity
has no opinion about the dam project
aciklama: 'What they rarely mention' ve 'One wonders whether ... worth such an irreversible cost' ifadeleri yazarın barajın yararlarından ciddi şüphe duyduğunu gösterir.

soru:
Recycling paper saves trees, but it also reduces energy use. Making paper from recycled material requires far less energy than producing it from fresh wood pulp. It also uses less water and creates less air pollution. Therefore, recycling paper benefits the environment in several ways.

What is the main idea of the passage?
secenekler: Recycling paper has a number of environmental benefits.
Paper production uses more water than any other industry.
Air pollution is mainly caused by paper factories.
Trees are the only source of paper.
Recycled paper is more expensive than new paper.
aciklama: Son cümle ana fikri özetler: kâğıt geri dönüşümü çevreye birçok açıdan yarar sağlar.

soru:
Many people think that bats are blind, but this is a myth. Most bats can see quite well. In addition, many species use echolocation: they produce high-pitched sounds and listen to the echoes to locate objects and insects in the dark. This combination of skills makes them excellent night hunters.

What is the main idea of the passage?
secenekler: Echolocation is used by humans as well as bats.
Bats only hunt during the day.
Insects are able to hear the sounds made by bats.
Bats have effective ways of finding their way and food in the dark.
aciklama: Parça yarasaların görme ve yankıyla yön bulma becerileri sayesinde iyi gece avcıları olduğunu anlatıyor.

soru:
In the past, a university degree almost guaranteed a secure job. Today, however, rapid technological change means that many skills become outdated within a few years. As a result, workers increasingly need to update their knowledge throughout their careers through short courses, online programmes and on-the-job training.

The main point of the passage is that ----.
secenekler: online programmes are better than university education
workers today are less educated than in the past
technology has made most jobs disappear
lifelong learning has become necessary in today's job market
university degrees are no longer offered by most institutions
aciklama: 'workers increasingly need to update their knowledge throughout their careers' cümlesi ana fikri verir.

soru:
Wetlands such as marshes and swamps were once regarded as useless land to be drained for farming. Scientists now know that they perform vital functions. They filter pollutants from water, absorb floodwater during heavy rains and provide habitats for many species of birds and fish. Protecting wetlands is therefore both an environmental and an economic priority.

What is the main idea of the passage?
secenekler: Pollution in wetlands cannot be reduced.
Wetlands are valuable ecosystems that deserve protection.
Floods are becoming more common because of heavy rains.
Wetlands should be drained to create more farmland.
Birds prefer marshes to other habitats.
aciklama: Parça sulak alanların işlevlerini sayıp korunmaları gerektiği sonucuna varıyor.

soru:
It is often assumed that creativity is a rare gift possessed by a few talented individuals. Research, however, suggests that creative thinking can be developed like any other skill. People who are regularly exposed to new ideas, who are encouraged to take risks and who are allowed to make mistakes tend to produce more original work, regardless of their initial ability.

What is the main idea of the passage?
secenekler: Creative people usually avoid taking risks.
Only a small number of people are born creative.
Creativity can be improved through the right conditions and practice.
Talented individuals do not need to practise.
Making mistakes always prevents original work.
aciklama: 'Research, however, suggests that creative thinking can be developed' cümlesi yaygın görüşü çürüterek ana fikri verir.

soru:
For much of the twentieth century, the stomach ulcer was blamed on stress and spicy food. In the 1980s, two Australian researchers challenged this view, arguing that most ulcers were caused by a bacterium. Their claim was initially dismissed by the medical establishment, but it was eventually confirmed, and the pair received the Nobel Prize in 2005. Today, most ulcers are cured with antibiotics.

The passage mainly discusses ----.
secenekler: the history of the Nobel Prize in medicine
the effects of stress on the human body
why spicy food is harmful to the stomach
how a widely held medical belief about ulcers was overturned
the dangers of using antibiotics too often
aciklama: Parça, ülserin nedenine dair yaygın inancın nasıl değiştiğini anlatıyor; Nobel ödülü yalnızca bir ayrıntıdır.

soru:
The Amazon River carries more water than any other river in the world. It flows for about 6,400 kilometres through several South American countries before reaching the Atlantic Ocean. During the rainy season, parts of the river can be more than 40 kilometres wide.

According to the passage, the Amazon River ----.
secenekler: is the shortest river in South America
is 40 kilometres wide throughout the year
is located in a single country
carries more water than any other river
aciklama: İlk cümle doğrudan cevaptır. Nehir Atlas Okyanusu'na dökülür ve 40 km genişlik yalnızca yağmur mevsimi içindir.

soru:
The first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens in 1896. Only 14 countries and about 240 athletes took part, and all of the competitors were men. Women were allowed to compete for the first time four years later, at the Paris Games of 1900.

It is stated in the passage that women ----.
secenekler: took part in the 1896 Games in Athens
first competed in the Olympic Games in 1900
were not allowed to compete until the 1920s
organised the first modern Olympic Games
made up half of the athletes in 1896
aciklama: Son cümle kadınların ilk kez dört yıl sonra, 1900 Paris Oyunları'nda yarıştığını söyler.

soru:
Tardigrades are tiny animals, less than a millimetre long, that can survive extreme conditions. When their environment dries out, they lose almost all the water in their bodies and enter a state similar to death. In this condition, they can withstand freezing temperatures, intense radiation and even the vacuum of space, returning to normal when water becomes available again.

According to the passage, when their environment dries out, tardigrades ----.
secenekler: lose most of the water in their bodies and become inactive
immediately die because of the lack of water
move to places where the temperature is warmer
grow to more than a millimetre in length
aciklama: 'they lose almost all the water in their bodies and enter a state similar to death' → vücut suyunu kaybedip hareketsiz hale gelirler; ölmezler.

soru:
The printing press, developed by Johannes Gutenberg around 1440, used movable metal type that could be arranged and rearranged to print different pages. Before its invention, books were copied by hand, a process that could take months. Within fifty years, printing presses had spread to more than 250 European cities.

Which of the following is stated in the passage?
secenekler: Movable type was made of wood.
Before the printing press, copying a book by hand could take months.
The printing press was used in only a few cities.
Printing presses reached Europe fifty years after they were invented in Asia.
aciklama: 'books were copied by hand, a process that could take months' cümlesi doğru seçeneği destekler; harfler metaldir ve matbaa 250'den fazla şehre yayılmıştır.

soru:
Although Venus is similar to Earth in size and mass, conditions on its surface are extremely hostile. Its thick atmosphere, composed mainly of carbon dioxide, traps heat so effectively that surface temperatures reach about 465°C, hot enough to melt lead. Clouds of sulphuric acid also cover the planet, reflecting most of the sunlight that reaches it.

According to the passage, the extremely high temperatures on Venus are mainly caused by ----.
secenekler: its thick carbon dioxide atmosphere trapping heat
the absence of clouds over the planet
its small size compared to Earth
its distance from the Sun being greater than Earth's
aciklama: 'Its thick atmosphere ... traps heat so effectively that surface temperatures reach about 465°C' → yüksek sıcaklığın nedeni ısıyı hapseden kalın atmosferdir.

soru:
Contrary to what their name suggests, killer whales are not whales but the largest members of the dolphin family. They live in close family groups called pods, which can include up to forty individuals. Each pod has its own distinctive set of calls, and young killer whales learn these calls from their mothers.

According to the passage, which of the following is true?
secenekler: A pod can include hundreds of individuals.
All pods use exactly the same calls.
Killer whales belong to the dolphin family.
Young killer whales learn their calls from other pods.
aciklama: İlk cümle katil balinaların yunus ailesinin en büyük üyeleri olduğunu söyler; diğer seçenekler metinle çelişir.

soru:
Emma checked the weather forecast before leaving home. She put on her raincoat, took her umbrella and wore her waterproof boots instead of her usual shoes.

It can be inferred from the passage that ----.
secenekler: Emma was going to the beach to sunbathe
the weather forecast was usually wrong
Emma did not own an umbrella
aciklama: Yağmurluk, şemsiye ve su geçirmez bot, tahminin yağmur olduğunu gösterir.

soru:
When the company introduced a four-day working week as an experiment, it expected productivity to fall. Instead, output remained the same, the number of sick days dropped by a third, and employees reported feeling less stressed. At the end of the trial, the management decided to make the change permanent.

It can be inferred from the passage that ----.
secenekler: productivity fell sharply during the experiment
the results of the trial were more positive than the company had expected
most employees wanted to return to a five-day week
employees worked longer hours during the trial
the management was unhappy with the results
aciklama: Şirket verimliliğin düşmesini beklerken 'Instead' ile olumlu sonuçlar sıralanır; sonuçlar beklenenden iyidir.

soru:
In some regions of the Arctic, the ground has been frozen for thousands of years. This frozen soil, known as permafrost, contains huge amounts of carbon from ancient plants. As global temperatures rise, the permafrost is beginning to thaw, and scientists are worried about what this could mean for the climate.

It can be inferred from the passage that ----.
secenekler: rising temperatures will cause the permafrost to expand
permafrost is found in every part of the world
thawing permafrost may release carbon that affects the climate
the Arctic has always been free of ice
ancient plants are still growing in the permafrost
aciklama: Permafrostun büyük miktarda karbon içermesi ve bilim insanlarının iklim açısından endişelenmesi, erimenin karbonu açığa çıkarabileceğini düşündürür.

soru:
Before the invention of refrigeration, people used a variety of methods to keep food from spoiling. Meat and fish were often dried, smoked or preserved in salt, while fruit was turned into jam. In winter, some wealthy families stored ice cut from frozen lakes in special underground buildings.

It can be inferred from the passage that ----.
secenekler: jam was invented after the refrigerator
salt was used only to preserve fruit
people did not eat meat before refrigeration
all families had underground ice houses
keeping food fresh was a challenge before refrigerators existed
aciklama: Çeşitli koruma yöntemlerinin geliştirilmesi, buzdolabından önce yiyecekleri taze tutmanın zor olduğunu gösterir.

soru:
Early explorers who reached the Pacific islands were surprised to find that sweet potatoes, a plant native to South America, were already being grown there. Since the islands lie thousands of kilometres from the American coast, some researchers have suggested that Polynesian sailors reached South America and brought the plant back long before Europeans arrived.

It can be inferred from the passage that ----.
secenekler: Polynesian sailors may have been capable of very long ocean voyages
early explorers brought sweet potatoes with them
sweet potatoes originally came from the Pacific islands
the Pacific islands are close to the American coast
Europeans introduced sweet potatoes to the Pacific islands
aciklama: Binlerce kilometrelik mesafeye rağmen bitkinin getirilmiş olabileceği görüşü, Polinezyalı denizcilerin çok uzun yolculuklar yapabildiğini düşündürür.

soru:
The city council installed speed cameras on the main road after a series of serious accidents. In the following year, the number of accidents on that road fell by 40 percent. However, accidents on the smaller streets nearby increased, as some drivers began using them to avoid the cameras.

It can be inferred from the passage that ----.
secenekler: drivers generally obeyed the speed limits on all roads
the cameras solved one problem but partly shifted it elsewhere
the speed cameras had no effect on accidents
the council removed the cameras after one year
the smaller streets were safer than the main road
aciklama: Ana yolda kazalar azalırken yan sokaklarda artması, sorunun kısmen başka yere kaydığını gösterir.

soru:
The hotel was so immense that it took us almost ten minutes to walk from our room to the restaurant.

The word 'immense' in the passage is closest in meaning to ----.
aciklama: Odadan restorana on dakika yürünmesi otelin çok büyük ('immense') olduğunu gösterir.

soru:
After the long hike in the heat, the children were famished and ate everything that was put in front of them.

The word 'famished' in the passage is closest in meaning to ----.
aciklama: 'ate everything that was put in front of them' ipucu çok aç ('famished') olduklarını gösterir.

soru:
The effects of the new policy were negligible: after a year, unemployment had fallen by only 0.1 percent, a change that most economists considered meaningless.

The word 'negligible' in the passage is closest in meaning to ----.
secenekler: so small as to be unimportant
aciklama: İki noktadan sonraki açıklama (yalnızca %0,1, anlamsız bir değişim) etkinin önemsiz derecede küçük olduğunu gösterir.

soru:
Scientists hope that the new treatment will mitigate the symptoms of the disease, even if it cannot cure it completely.

The word 'mitigate' in the passage is closest in meaning to ----.
aciklama: 'even if it cannot cure it completely' tam tedavi olmasa da belirtileri hafifletmeyi ('mitigate' = reduce) anlatır.

soru:
The author's argument is quite plausible; the evidence she presents is consistent and her reasoning is easy to follow.

The word 'plausible' in the passage is closest in meaning to ----.
aciklama: Tutarlı kanıt ve kolay izlenen akıl yürütme, argümanın inandırıcı ('plausible') olduğunu gösterir.

soru:
Although the company's chief executive was initially adamant that no jobs would be lost, he was eventually forced to announce hundreds of redundancies.

The word 'adamant' in the passage is closest in meaning to ----.
aciklama: 'Although ... eventually forced' zıtlığı, yöneticinin başta kesin bir tutumla ('adamant' = kararlı, ısrarlı) iş kaybı olmayacağını söylediğini gösterir.

soru:
Our new fitness app makes exercising fun! Track your progress, join friendly challenges and get personalised workout plans. Download it today and enjoy your first month for free.

The main purpose of the passage is to ----.
secenekler: warn about the dangers of exercise
aciklama: 'Download it today', 'first month for free' gibi ifadeler metnin bir ürünü tanıtıp satmaya çalıştığını gösterir.

soru:
Some critics claim that video games are nothing more than a waste of time. This view ignores a growing body of research showing that certain games can improve problem-solving skills, reaction times and even cooperation between players. Dismissing all games as harmful is, quite simply, unfair.

The author's attitude towards the critics is ----.
aciklama: 'This view ignores...' ve 'quite simply, unfair' ifadeleri yazarın eleştirmenlere karşı olumsuz (disapproving) tutumunu gösterir.

soru:
The novel's plot moves slowly, and some of the minor characters are rather forgettable. Nevertheless, the author's vivid descriptions of life in a small fishing village and her deep understanding of human relationships make the book well worth reading.

The writer's overall opinion of the novel is ----.
secenekler: unclear because no reasons are given
critical of its descriptions of village life
aciklama: 'Nevertheless ... well worth reading' ifadesi zayıflıklara rağmen genel görüşün olumlu olduğunu gösterir.
